                           UNITED STATES DISTRICT COURT
                         NORTHERN DISTRICT OF CALIFORNIA

                                        CIVIL MINUTES

 Date: 8/29/2025                  Time: 3:05 p.m. - 3:37 p.m.  Judge: EUMI K. LEE
                                  (Total Time: 32 minutes)
 Case No.: 25-cv-07105-EKL        Case Name: Apple Inc. v. Shi

Attorney for Plaintiff: Adam Alper, Mike DeVries, Leslie Schmidt, Laura Vartain, Maria
Beltran, Adina Stohl, Diek Van Nort
Attorney for Defendant: For Dr. Shi: Annabel Chang, For Oppo: Robyn Crowther, Sara
Morse, Grace Wong; For InnoPeak: Randy Kay, Jennifer Bennet, Richard Wahng

 Deputy Clerk: Laura Thomson                            Court Reporter: Summer Fisher


                           PROCEEDINGS and MINUTE ORDER

The Court held a status conference and set the following schedule, as described further below:

 Event                                                                 Deadline
 Meet and confer and file update regarding Magistrate Judge            September 5, 2025
 consent
 Meet and confer and submit joint statement regarding scope of         September 12, 2025
 discovery and any disputes
 Defendants respond to discovery requests                              September 25, 2025
 Defendants produce responsive documents                               October 9, 2025
 Complete depositions and file status report for conference            October 23, 2025
 Status conference                                                     October 29, 2025
 File motion for preliminary injunction                                November 5, 2025
 File opposition to motion for preliminary injunction                  November 19, 2025
 File reply in support of motion for preliminary injunction            November 26, 2025
 Preliminary injunction hearing (specific date to be set)              Week of December 15,
                                                                       2025

By September 5, 2025, if all parties stipulate to Magistrate Judge jurisdiction pursuant to 28
U.S.C. § 636(c), the parties shall file a letter informing the Court and specifying the parties’
preferred Magistrate Judge, if any. Each party shall also file the Consent or Declination to
Magistrate Judge Jurisdiction Form available at https://cand.uscourts.gov/mj_consent-
declination_form_10-2020/, indicating their consent.

The parties shall promptly meet and confer regarding the scope of expedited discovery. By
September 12, 2025, the parties shall file a joint statement regarding the scope of discovery and
any disputes that need resolution, setting forth the parties’ respective positions. The statement
        Case 5:25-cv-07105-EKL           Document 41       Filed 08/29/25      Page 2 of 2




shall address whether a stay of discovery as to Defendant Shi is appropriate at this stage. The
scope of discovery to be completed by the deadlines set forth above is subject to the parties’
meet and confer efforts and rulings on discovery disputes, if any.

If any party needs additional time to complete discovery, the relevant parties shall meet and
confer to reach agreement on a reasonable extension. If agreement cannot be reached, the party
may file an administrative motion establishing good cause for the requested extension.

A further status conference is set for October 29, 2025, at 1:30 p.m. via Zoom video. In
advance of this status conference, the parties shall meet and confer regarding whether
preliminary injunction proceedings are necessary, and if so, their scope. If the parties can reach
agreement on an extension and/or modification of interim relief, and upon the parties’ request,
the Court will vacate the preliminary injunction deadlines set forth above.

IT IS SO ORDERED.

Dated: August 29, 2025                                           EUMI K. LEE
                                                                 United States District Judge

 1          Plaintiff Apple Inc. (“Apple”), Defendant Chen Shi (“Dr. Shi”), Defendant Guangdong Oppo
 2   Mobile Telecommunications Corp., Ltd. (“OPPO”), and Defendant InnoPeak Technology, Inc.
 3   (“InnoPeak”), by and through their respective undersigned counsel, hereby submit the following joint
 4   status report, pursuant to the Court’s August 26, 2025 Order approving the parties’ Joint Status Report
 5   (Dkt. 31). Pursuant to the agreement of the parties and Court Order, the parties submit this joint statement
 6   on the two required issues for submission: (1) proposed schedule for preliminary injunction proceedings;
 7   (2) expedited discovery, and set out their respective positions below.
 8   I.     Proposed Schedule for Preliminary Injunction Proceedings
 9
            A.      Apple’s Statement
10

11          The Proposed Order that Apple submitted in connection with its Ex Parte Application for a
12   Temporary Restraining Order requested Defendants be enjoined from disclosing, retaining, or using “any
13   Apple confidential information or trade secrets.” At the guidance of the Court, and in an effort to halt the
14   most egregious aspects of Defendants theft, Apple agreed to a narrower provision that was limited to the
15   specific files listed in Attachment A to the order and other Apple materials that Defendants identified in
16   their investigation. The theft in this case, however, goes beyond that information, as Apple’s complaint
17   and TRO made clear. Dkt. 1 ¶¶ 7, 10, 72-75; Dkt. 11 at 2, 6-8, 13-15 (describing 1:1 meetings that Dr.
18   Shi set up under false pretenses to induce Apple employees to share trade-secret information). As such,
19   expedited discovery, in combination with a preliminary injunction, is critical to fully protect Apple’s trade
20   secrets during the pendency of this action.
21          On August 28, 2025, the parties submitted their joint status report (Dkt. 29), which the Court
22   approved. Dkt. 31. In the joint status report, the parties stated: “The parties jointly request that they be
23   permitted to provide a proposed briefing schedule” for a preliminary injunction “on Thursday, August
24   28, 2025.” Dkt. 31 at 1 (emphasis added). The Court’s stipulated interim measures order even recognizes
25   “Apple’s forthcoming preliminary injunction motion.” (Dkt. 30 at 2.) The parties also jointly told the
26   Court that “[t]he parties are in agreement that expedited discovery will be conducted and that it begins
27   immediately.” Dkt. 31 at 1. (emphasis added). Defendants now backtrack and refuse to agree to a briefing
28   schedule or participate in expedited discovery. Apple negotiated and agreed to the interim relief ordered

     JOINT STATUS REPORT                                1                      CASE NO. 5:25-CV-07105-EKL
             Case 5:25-cv-07105-EKL           Document 38        Filed 08/28/25      Page 3 of 16



 1   by the Court (Dkt. 31) based on Defendants’ representations during Monday’s hearing and the subsequent
 2   meet and confer process, and respectfully requests that the Court enter a briefing schedule for a
 3   preliminary injunction (discussed in this section) and for expedited discovery (discussed in the section
 4   below).
 5          Defendants’ transparent attempts to delay this case, and obstruct Apple’s ability to ascertain
 6   whether the interim relief is sufficient, should be rejected.1 Defendants contend that the Court should
 7   divert from traditional steps in circumstances like this where there is evidence of a massive theft—i.e.,
 8   expedited discovery followed by a preliminary injunction briefing and hearing—and instead pause all
 9   such activities. InnoPeak and OPPO already had their chance to stop the theft when Dr. Shi told them that
10   he was going to collect Apple confidential information for use at his new job with Defendants. But instead,
11   as set out in detail in Apple’s complaint and TRO, they encouraged it. Dkt. 1 at 2, 17-18 ;Dkt. 11-1 at 8,
12   13-14. As such, Defendants should not be permitted to be the sole arbiter of their own malfeasance, while
13   Apple’s confidential information is further disseminated through Defendants’ organizations. Indeed, Dr.
14   Shi has been communicating with Defendants about Apple confidential information for months, and has
15   been working onsite with Defendants since at least June. Tellingly, Defendants claim that the existing
16   interim relief provides adequate relief, but admit that they have not materially begun any investigation to
17   be in a position to determine if that is true. Defendants also fail to appreciate the terms and force of the
18   interim relief, further demonstrating the need for a preliminary injunction and discovery. Innopeak, for
19   example, claims that it is taking actions “to remediate any Apple information deserving of remediation, if
20   any (Stipulation at pages 2-3).” The interim relief, however, does not permit Defendants to deem what
21   “Apple information” is worthy of “remediation” (presumably, Innopeak means “quarantine” and not
22   “remove” by its use of “remediate,” as that would be contrary to the interim relief). OPPO also claims
23   that there is “nothing left to brief” because Apple has not sufficiently identified what other information is
24   in Defendants’ possession, but that is precisely why expedited discovery is necessary—to determine what
25   additional measures are necessary to protect Apple’s intellectual property.
26          Accordingly, Apple proposes the following schedule for proceedings on its forthcoming motion
27   1
         Innopeak was served today, and Apple will file the summons as soon as the proof of service is
28       finalized.


     JOINT STATUS REPORT                                2                      CASE NO. 5:25-CV-07105-EKL
             Case 5:25-cv-07105-EKL           Document 38         Filed 08/28/25      Page 4 of 16



 1   for preliminary injunction. The schedule follows the briefing schedule and page limits in the Local Rules.
 2   To the extent that Defendants file separate opposition briefs, Apple will endeavor to file a single reply
 3   within the page limits, but respectfully requests that it be permitted to file separate replies if it is not
 4   feasible to file a single, 15-page reply in response to separate briefing from Defendants.

13

14

15
     with this position.
16

17
     requires time to analyze and resolve, and he believes that providing responses to written discovery by
18
     October 17, 2025, is sufficient, while depositions are premature.
19

20          C.      OPPO’s Statement
21
            OPPO has not reneged on any agreement that it made with Apple. To the contrary, OPPO has
22
     offered to extend that agreement until further order of the Court. For its part, Apple is unable to
23
     articulate any additional relief to which it might be entitled now that the interim relief is in place.
24
     Unwilling to take yes for an answer, Apple has instead misrepresented OPPO’s position and insisted
25

26   upon unrealistic and unnecessary deadlines. Apple asserts that OPPO and the other Defendants should

27   not be permitted to investigate the claims Apple has made before engaging in the discovery process
28

 1   because it would be prejudicial and inequitable for them to do so. That is nonsensical: Any party to a
 2   lawsuit must investigate the opposing party’s claims before responding to discovery requests.
 3
             It is unclear how Apple believes a corporate entity such as OPPO (without tens of thousands of
 4
     employees) would go about responding to questions about actions of one or two individuals that it
 5
     learned about less than two weeks ago. What Apple attempts to characterize as nefarious conduct is just
 6

 7   fact gathering that any party to litigation must do before responding to questions under oath. That is why

 8   Parties – whether individuals or entities – generally have a minimum of 30 days to respond to discovery

 9   requests. To the extent that the factual investigation allowed the opportunity for misconduct, there are
10

11

12

13

 1           If those agreements are extended, OPPO believes Apple’s request for further preliminary
 2   injunctive relief is mooted. The Proposed Order Apple submitted with its TRO Application sought three
 3
     specific things:
 4
         1. To enjoin Defendants from “disclosing, retaining or using any Apple confidential information or

28

 1   II.    Plaintiff’s Request for Expedited Discovery, as Detailed in the TRO Motion
 2          A.      Apple’s Statement
 3
            In the Joint Status Report approved by the Court (Dkt. 31), the parties stated that they “are in
 4
     agreement that expedited discovery will be conducted and that it begins immediately.” Following
 5
     submission of that agreement to the Court, Plaintiff served narrowed discovery on Defendants, in the form
 6
     of interrogatories (4 to each defendant), requests for production (4 to each defendant), deposition notices
 7
     to Drs. Shi and Zeng, and a 30(b)(6) notice to the corporate defendants (8 topics). See Exhibit A. Apple’s
 8
     discovery is not, as OPPO claims “full merits discovery.” It is narrowly tailored, and Apple narrowed its
 9
     interrogatories and requests for production from what it submitted with the TRO. Regardless, if OPPO
10
     believed Apple’s discovery was too broad, it could have conferred with Apple on that point, but it did not.
11
     Despite Defendants’ representations to Apple and the Court, Defendants now will not engage in expedited
12
     discovery. And Defendants refused to provide any schedule for that discovery at all, and instead are
13
     insisting that they be permitted to conduct their own, internal investigation, on their own time frame,
14
     before providing Apple any information into the extent of the theft through an expedited discovery
15
     process. Allowing Defendants to conduct a unilateral investigation into their own malfeasance while
16
     depriving Apple of the ability to use the discovery processes provided by the Federal Rules of Civil
17
     Procedure to discover the full extent of the theft prior to preliminary injunction proceeding would severely
18
     prejudice Apple. Apple respectfully requests that the Court order expedited discovery, as the parties
19
     initially agreed, and submits that there is good cause to do so, as set out below.
20
            Expedited discovery is routinely ordered in cases such as this, where there is direct evidence of
21
     serious acts of misappropriation. This is necessary here: to date, Apple has been able to uncover at least
22
     part of the Defendants’ scheme to steal Apple’s trade secrets and use that information to the OPPO
23
     Defendants’ benefit. Despite the strong indications that Defendants engaged in very serious acts of
24
     misappropriation—including the fact that Defendants put Dr. Shi and another Oppo employee on leave,—
25

26
